paper.one_line_finding: In Study 1 (486 analyzed), expert-rated idea quality rose over the no-AI control with model-led rewriting (3.11 vs 2.68, t(481) = 3.86, d = 0.55) and question-mode (2.96, t(481) = 2.49, d = 0.36) but not with vanilla GPT-4.1 chat (2.70, d = 0.02) or suggestion-mode (2.78, d = 0.13), and question-mode ideas were more diverse than model-led ideas (0.379 vs 0.309, d = 0.76; no AI-versus-control diversity test) (p. 12, Tables 2-3).

arms.name: Question-mode (Q)
arms.description: Human-led question mode: the participant supplies an initial unassisted idea; GPT-4.1 supplies knowledge or an analogy and asks questions to elicit alternatives, then asks elaboration questions before the participant submits the refined idea. This follows the Table 5 prompts and Figure 2; Section 4.2 instead describes the model as generating the alternatives.

arms.name: Suggestion-mode (S)
arms.description: Human-led suggestion mode: GPT-4.1 supplies alternative ideas and elaboration suggestions after an unassisted initial idea; the participant refines and submits the final idea.

arms.name: Model-led (M)
arms.description: Model-led one-shot refinement: GPT-4.1 rewrites the participant initial idea to increase originality, usefulness and elaboration; the participant may further refine the model output before submission.

arms.name: Vanilla (V)
arms.description: Free chat with GPT-4.1 in the same chat interface, without additional system prompts or intervention logic; participants could formulate or copy and paste the final idea.

arms.name: Control (C)
arms.description: Participants generate and refine their idea without LLM support.

studies.task: Generate and refine one creative idea repurposing existing car features for new uses beyond their original purpose in vehicles.

ai_tool.name: GPT-4.1 via the OpenAI API (snapshot gpt-4.1-2025-04-14)
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 6, Section 4.2: all LLM-assisted conditions used GPT-4.1, snapshot gpt-4.1-2025-04-14; PDF p. 19, Table 5 note. The Vanilla row in Table 5 inconsistently says Standard GPT-4.

preregistration.primary_outcome: Idea quality, diversity of the idea pool, and perceived idea ownership are the primary outcomes named in PDF p. 7, Section 4.4, with preregistered hypotheses in Sections 3 and 4.5. The paper does not rank one above the others.

estimates.outcome: Idea quality (expert mean of originality and usefulness)
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Consensual Assessment Technique: four domain experts independently rated originality and usefulness on seven-point scales; ratings across dimensions and raters were averaged to one score per idea. Each participant supplied one scored idea (only the first idea was judged if more than one was supplied). PDF p. 7, Section 4.4; PDF p. 22, Appendix D.

(PDF p. 7, Section 4.2, Vanilla LLM description; pp. 7-8, Section 4.5; p. 12, Tables 2 and 3 (H1d); p. 25, Appendix H.1, Table 14.: "Participants could freely chat with GPT 4.1 and formulate or copy and paste the idea they generated.")

estimates.outcome: Idea diversity (cosine distance to leave-one-out condition centroid)
estimates.question: across_people
estimates.measure_detail: OpenAI text-embedding-3-large; per-idea cosine distance to the leave-one-out centroid of the other final ideas within the same experimental condition. Higher distance means greater across-person diversity. One scored final idea per participant. PDF p. 7, Section 4.4; PDF p. 8, footnote 2.

estimates.notes: Arm means, SDs and analyzed people counts are transcribed from Table 2. SDs are across the scored outputs, one output per participant, so output-level and participant-level variation coincide here. Section 4.4 defines cosine distance and the results interpret higher values as more diverse, despite similarity terminology in the Table 2 note and Appendix H. estimates.primary_override_reason: Rule 2: The introduction's stated contribution contrasts question-driven interaction with model-led refinement on diversity. The corresponding untransformed linear-model contrast in Table 3 is the main specification; Appendix H explicitly presents logit and Dunn alternatives as robustness checks. (PDF p. 3, Section 1 (Introduction), contribution (1); pp. 7-8, Section 4.5; p. 12, Table 3 (H2a); p. 25, Appendix H.1, Table 15.: "model-led idea refinement improves idea quality at the cost of idea diversity and perceived idea ownership. In contrast, actively involving participants with a question-driven interaction mode produces high-quality ideas while preserving ownership and even enhancing diversity.")

estimates.measure_detail: OpenAI text-embedding-3-large; per-idea cosine distance to the leave-one-out centroid of the other final ideas within the same experimental condition. estimates.notes: Contrast-specific totals are not printed; counts have not been summed. Section 4.4 defines cosine distance and the results interpret higher values as more diverse, despite similarity terminology in the Table 2 note and Appendix H. The paper treats each person once in the main analysis, but the distances share condition centroids; it does not report uncertainty that recomputes those centroids under participant resampling. Alternative specification of the same sample and primary diversity outcome. No arm mean, SD, SE, raw difference, or confidence interval on the logit scale is printed, so those fields are null. Original cosine-distance means and SDs are retained in s1_diversity_question_mode_vs_vanilla; they are not mixed with the transformed test here. The table provides t, degrees of freedom, p and Cohen’s d; the d standardizer is not stated. preregistered_primary refers to the outcome, not to this robustness specification.

estimates.outcome: Between-arm difference in initial-to-refined idea-diversity change
estimates.question: across_people
estimates.measure_detail: OpenAI text-embedding-3-large cosine distance: initial and refined ideas are evaluated against the centroid of initial ideas in their own condition, with leave-one-out initial distances. The outcome is the change from the unassisted initial idea to the refined idea produced with AI available. Both arm means below are estimated mean changes, not final-idea levels. PDF pp. 8-9, Section 5.3 and footnote 2; PDF p. 10, Figure 6; PDF p. 24, Tables 12-13.

stats.difference_is: As printed: control minus treatment in change, namely (Model-led (M): refined minus initial) minus (Question-mode (Q): refined minus initial). The regression coefficient, t-statistic, and CI retain this printed orientation.

regression.model: Linear mixed-effects model of idea diversity with interaction mode, time and mode-by-time interactions; Question-Mode and initial idea are reference levels, with a participant random intercept. The recorded term is Model-Led × Time. It estimates the named control-arm change minus the Question-mode treatment-arm change.

sources.locator: PDF p. 24, Appendix G, Table 13, Question-mode row (Change and SE)
PDF p. 24, Appendix G, Table 13, Model-led (M) row (Change and SE)
PDF p. 24, Appendix G, Table 12, Model-Led × Time fixed-effect row
PDF p. 24, Appendix G, Table 12, interval-column heading

estimates.notes: Exploratory comparison of change between individually randomized AI arms; this is not a randomized-order crossover. within_person is null because the qualifying comparison is between randomized arms. The initial-to-refined order is fixed. The paper does not print the sample size for this mixed model; no counts are inferred from degrees of freedom or borrowed from Table 2. Question-mode is the tested human-led configuration and is named treatment as in the screening form. IMPORTANT SIGN: Table 12 uses Question-Mode as the regression reference and prints the other arm minus Question-Mode. The coefficient, t-statistic and CI retain this printed sign, which is the reverse of treatment minus control. difference_is explicitly records that orientation; no sign has been calculated or changed. Arm levels and arm SEs come from Table 13 and are estimated refined-minus-initial changes. The interaction coefficient and its uncertainty come from Table 12; arm changes have not been subtracted. The mean-change levels in Table 13 are not interchangeable with final-idea centroid distances in Table 2. The model includes participant random intercepts, but the condition-centroid dependence is not explicitly addressed.

open_items: Study 2 randomization, recruitment details, and per-arm participant counts are not stated. Eligibility is unconfirmed for that study; no Study 2 estimates are extracted (PDF pp. 10-11, Section 6.1).

Study 1 arm-level counts at randomization are not printed. Section 4 describes the randomized experiment as N = 502 (PDF p. 5), and Section 4.3 reports final N = 486 after exclusions (PDF p. 7); the abstract instead labels the randomized experiment N = 486 (PDF p. 1). The study record uses the recruited/assigned count and final analyzed count separately.

Main planned contrasts have no printed contrast SEs or CIs, although Section 4.5 promises confidence intervals (PDF p. 8). Table 2 supplies raw arm means and SDs; no differences, totals, SEs, or CIs are derived here.
The paper does not state the standardizer used for Cohen's d or for the Dunn r effect sizes (PDF p. 8, Section 4.5; PDF pp. 12 and 25, Tables 3, 14-15).
For diversity H2b, Table 3 prints p = .984 (PDF p. 12) while Section 5.1.2 prints p = .983 (PDF p. 8). The table value is extracted; neither is silently corrected.
For diversity H3a, Table 3 prints d = 0.27 (PDF p. 12) while Section 5.1.2 prints d = 0.29 (PDF p. 8). The table value is extracted.

Diversity is explicitly cosine distance in Section 4.4 (PDF p. 7), but Table 2 and Appendix H use similarity terminology (PDF pp. 12 and 25). Direction is coded more_diverse based on the definition and interpretation. Shared-centroid dependence is not addressed by the printed uncertainty.
No transformed arm means or SDs are printed for the logit robustness tests in Table 15 (PDF p. 25); these are left null. Their main-specification counterparts retain raw cosine-distance levels.

The exploratory diversity-change model does not print its participant sample size or per-arm counts (PDF pp. 9 and 24). Counts are not inferred from degrees of freedom or borrowed from Table 2. No initial/final arm levels or change SDs are printed; Table 13 supplies estimated arm changes and SEs.

The diversity-change interaction coefficients and CIs use Question-mode as the reference (PDF p. 24, Table 12). With Question-mode designated treatment, they are printed control-minus-treatment estimates. Their signs must be interpreted using difference_is and the model description; all printed signs are preserved.

Within-arm change reporting is inconsistent: Question-mode t = 7.24 and upper CI = 0.085 in Table 12 versus t = 7.20 and upper CI = 0.086 in Table 13 (PDF p. 24); Suggestion-mode t = -2.67 in Section 5.3 (PDF p. 9) versus -2.78 in Table 13. Those before-after tests are excluded; the extracted randomized interaction rows retain Table 12 coefficients and Table 13 arm mean changes/SEs.

The Question-mode description says the LLM generated alternatives (PDF p. 6, Section 4.2), whereas the Table 5 prompts ask participants to generate alternatives (PDF p. 19). The study-level AI role is other because roles differ across arms.

Table 5 calls Vanilla Standard GPT-4, while the note and Section 4.2 explicitly specify GPT-4.1 for all AI conditions (PDF pp. 6 and 19). The tool record follows the explicit common-model statement and dated snapshot.
